---
title: "Luka Dončić: a reproducible warehouse example"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
---

The bundled sample contains three real 2024–25 games. It is an infrastructure
demonstration, not an estimate of season-long or defensive ability.

```{r}
# Render from the project root: quarto render articles/luka-efficiency.qmd
project_root <- if (file.exists('scripts/load.R')) '.' else '..'
withr::with_dir(project_root, {
  source('scripts/load.R')
  con <- connect_warehouse('data/processed/article-demo.duckdb')
  ingest_bundle(con, readRDS('data/sample/bundle.rds'), '2024-25')
  games <- get_player_games('Luka Doncic', '2024-25', con)
  result <- offensive_efficiency(games)
  DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
  knitr::kable(result, digits = 3)
})
```

Effective FG% weights made threes by 1.5. True shooting uses the conventional
0.44 free-throw coefficient, an approximation rather than observed possessions.
The warehouse preserves raw records and provider attribution. A six-attempt
matchup omits free throws, passes, turnovers and selection effects; it cannot
establish a defender's underlying ability.

The warehouse also reconstructs possessions and five-player stints against a
separate NBA-derived totals fixture. These do not identify a responsible defender.

```{r}
withr::with_dir(project_root, {
  con <- connect_warehouse('data/processed/article-demo.duckdb')
  import_reference(con, load_reference_fixture())
  reconcile_game_totals(con)
  reconstruct_season(con, '2024-25')
  assert_warehouse_integrity(con)
  checks <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste(
    'SELECT s.game_id, s.possessions_status, s.lineups_status,',
    '(SELECT count(*) FROM possessions p WHERE p.game_id=s.game_id) possessions,',
    '(SELECT count(*) FROM lineups l WHERE l.game_id=s.game_id) team_stints',
    'FROM reconstruction_status s ORDER BY s.game_id'
  ))
  DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
  knitr::kable(checks)
})
```

Technical and retained-possession FT points are separate. Possession points
plus those points must equal the score. Stints require five unique players,
complete period coverage and minute reconciliation. Failed games remain
unresolved rather than receiving guessed players or defender roles.
